ios.desc:
Never be the last to know about a cloud outage.

Upti monitors the status of major cloud providers and SaaS platforms in real-time — all in one place. No more checking multiple status pages. Open Upti and see what's up and what's down, instantly.

SUPPORTED CATEGORIES
•⁠  ⁠Cloud Providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, and more)
•⁠  ⁠CI/CD Platforms
•⁠  ⁠Databases
•⁠  ⁠CDN Services
•⁠  ⁠Monitoring Tools
•⁠  ⁠Communication Platforms
•⁠  ⁠Container Registries
•⁠  ⁠AI Services
•⁠  ⁠And more being added regularly

WHY UPTI?
•⁠  ⁠One dashboard for all your services
•⁠  ⁠Real-time status updates at a glance
•⁠  ⁠Organized by category for easy browsing
•⁠  ⁠Detailed uptime history (24h, 7d, 30d)
•⁠  ⁠Direct links to official status pages
•⁠  ⁠Customize your watchlist — track only what matters
•⁠  ⁠Clean, native iOS design
•⁠  ⁠Lightweight and fast
•⁠  ⁠No accounts, no sign-up required

PERFECT FOR
•⁠  ⁠DevOps engineers monitoring infrastructure
•⁠  ⁠SREs tracking service dependencies
•⁠  ⁠Developers debugging "is it down?" moments
•⁠  ⁠IT managers reporting outage impact
•⁠  ⁠Anyone who depends on cloud services

When AWS goes down, you'll know before your boss asks.

Stay informed. Stay ahead. Stay Upti.

quotes.text:
Hi HN! I built Upti, a small app that monitors major cloud provider status pages and notifies you when there are outages/incidents.

  Why I made it:  
  - I wanted a simple way to track service disruptions across providers in one place  
  - Official status pages are useful but fragmented  
  - I needed quick, actionable notifications  

  What Upti does:  
  - Scrapes provider status/incident pages  
  - Sends outage/incident alerts  
  - Keeps the experience lightweight and fast  

  I’d love feedback on:  
  - Which providers/services I should prioritize next  
  - Alert quality (too noisy vs too late)  
  - What would make this genuinely useful for SRE/DevOps workflows  

  Happy to share implementation details if useful.
